what_its_for: Linaclotide is used to treat two conditions in adults: irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C) and chronic idiopathic constipation (CIC), which means long-term constipation with no known cause. It works by helping your intestines move stool along and reducing pain and discomfort in your belly.
how_to_take: Take linaclotide by mouth, on an EMPTY stomach, at least 30 minutes BEFORE your first meal of the day. Swallow the capsule whole with water. Do NOT crush, break, or chew the capsule. If you have trouble swallowing capsules, you may open the capsule and sprinkle the tiny beads inside onto a teaspoon of room-temperature applesauce or into a small cup of room-temperature water (about 30 mL), then swallow right away without chewing the beads. Do NOT save the mixture for later.
dosing: Your doctor will prescribe the dose that is right for your condition. The typical adult doses are: For IBS-C (irritable bowel syndrome with constipation): 290 micrograms (mcg) once daily. For CIC (chronic idiopathic constipation): 72 mcg or 145 mcg once daily. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time the following day. Do NOT take two doses on the same day to make up for the one you missed. Taking a double dose can increase your risk of serious side effects like severe diarrhea.
storage: Store linaclotide at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep the capsules in their ORIGINAL container with the lid tightly closed. Do NOT remove the desiccant packet (the small packet inside the bottle that absorbs moisture) — leave it in the bottle at all times. Keep the bottle away from moisture and heat. Do NOT store it in the bathroom. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Accidental ingestion by a child can be very dangerous.
what_to_avoid: Do NOT give linaclotide to children under 2 years of age — it can be life-threatening. Avoid giving it to children under 18 years old unless specifically directed by a doctor. Avoid taking linaclotide if you have a bowel blockage (intestinal obstruction), as it can make this condition worse. Do not take it with a meal, as food can increase side effects like diarrhea. Avoid alcohol in excess, as it can worsen stomach upset. Do not stop taking the medication without talking to your doctor first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency care if you experience: severe diarrhea that does not stop, signs of dehydration such as extreme thirst, dizziness, lightheadedness, urinating less than normal, or feeling faint, blood in your stool, severe stomach pain or cramping, or worsening of your symptoms. Also call your doctor if you become pregnant, are planning to become pregnant, or are breastfeeding while taking this medication.
when_it_works: Some people notice improvement in their bowel movements within the first 1 to 2 weeks of treatment. Relief from belly pain and bloating may take a little longer. If you do not notice any improvement after a few weeks, let your doctor know. Do not stop taking the medication on your own without speaking with your doctor first.
special_populations: Children: Linaclotide must NOT be used in children under 2 years old and is not recommended for children under 18 years old. Pregnancy: It is not known if linaclotide is safe to use during pregnancy. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: It is unknown if linaclotide passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while on this medication. Older adults (65+): No specific dose adjustment is needed, but older adults should be monitored closely for dehydration if diarrhea occurs. Kidney or liver problems: No dose adjustment is generally needed, but always tell your doctor about all your medical conditions.
